hints.title: Streak Interruption Conditions
hints.text: A consecutive increasing streak breaks whenever the transaction date is not exactly one day after the previous date or the amount does not strictly increase.

hints.title: Window Streak Identification
hints.text: Use lag window functions to examine the preceding transaction date and amount for each customer, flagging break points to assign unique streak group IDs.

hints.title: Streak Length Filter
hints.text: Group by customer and streak identifier, filter for groups with at least three transactions, and compute the earliest and latest dates.

hints.title: Gaps and Islands Window Query Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH Flagged AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        transaction_date,
        amount,
        LAG(transaction_date, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS prev_date,
        LAG(amount, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS prev_amount
    FROM Transactions
),
Graded AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        transaction_date,
        amount,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN prev_date IS NULL OR DATEDIFF(transaction_date, prev_date) > 1 OR amount <= prev_amount THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS streak_id
    FROM Flagged
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(transaction_date) AS consecutive_start,
    MAX(transaction_date) AS consecutive_end
FROM Graded
GROUP BY customer_id, streak_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY customer_id ASC, consecutive_start ASC, consecutive_end ASC;
```

complexity.time: O(N log N) for partitioned window sort
complexity.notes: Gaps and islands grouping using LAG and cumulative sum of streak breaks.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Multi-day self-joins fail to handle arbitrarily long variable-length streaks.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) memory for streak partitioning buffer.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulates gaps and islands with window functions and filters streaks of length >= 3.

WITH Flagged AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        transaction_date,
        amount,
        LAG(transaction_date, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS prev_date,
        LAG(amount, 1) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS prev_amount
    FROM Transactions
),
Graded AS (
    SELECT
        customer_id,
        transaction_date,
        amount,
        SUM(
            CASE
                WHEN prev_date IS NULL OR (transaction_date::date - prev_date::date) > 1 OR amount <= prev_amount THEN 1
                ELSE 0
            END
        ) OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY transaction_date) AS streak_id
    FROM Flagged
)
SELECT
    customer_id,
    MIN(transaction_date) AS consecutive_start,
    MAX(transaction_date) AS consecutive_end
FROM Graded
GROUP BY customer_id, streak_id
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 3
ORDER BY customer_id ASC, consecutive_start ASC, consecutive_end ASC;

import pandas as pd

def consecutive_increasing_transactions(transactions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    transactions['transaction_date'] = pd.to_datetime(transactions['transaction_date'])
    transactions = transactions.sort_values(by=['customer_id', 'transaction_date']).reset_index(drop=True)
    prev_date = transactions.groupby('customer_id')['transaction_date'].shift(1)
    prev_amount = transactions.groupby('customer_id')['amount'].shift(1)
    break_streak = prev_date.isna() | ((transactions['transaction_date'] - prev_date).dt.days > 1) | (transactions['amount'] <= prev_amount)
    transactions['streak_id'] = break_streak.cumsum()
    grouped = transactions.groupby(['customer_id', 'streak_id']).agg(
        consecutive_start=('transaction_date', 'min'),
        consecutive_end=('transaction_date', 'max'),
        cnt=('transaction_date', 'count')
    ).reset_index()
    res = grouped[grouped['cnt'] >= 3][['customer_id', 'consecutive_start', 'consecutive_end']]
    return res.sort_values(by=['customer_id', 'consecutive_start', 'consecutive_end'])
